themes_detail.label: Street Sign Disappearance Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street signs are vanishing across Flushing at an unprecedented rate—10 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks (789% spike, z-score 9.57), creating navigation hazards and potential traffic safety risks amid heavy pedestrian and vehicle volume.
evidence: 10 missing street sign complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (789% increase, z-score 9.57)
Highest z-score spike in entire dataset indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Flushing's dense commercial and residential corridors (Northern Boulevard, Main Street) heavily dependent on wayfinding signage
reporting_angles: Interview DOT about sign theft/vandalism patterns and enforcement response in Flushing's high-traffic commercial corridors
Speak with elderly residents and new immigrants who rely on street signs for navigation in multilingual neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Street and Sidewalk Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints spiked 317% LAST WEEK to 12 filings versus a baseline of 2.9 per week (z-score 6.28), indicating accelerating pavement failure and underground infrastructure stress across the district.
evidence: 12 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints filed last week vs. 2.9 weekly baseline (317% increase, z-score 6.28)
Community board has repeatedly budgeted requests for water main inspection/repair on specific street segments—unresolved multi-year pattern
Spike preceded only by street sign crisis and noise complaints in recency ranking
reporting_angles: Investigate DEP's backlog on water main repairs in Flushing; cross-reference budget requests vs. actual capital spending over 3+ years
Document specific block segments with repeated complaints; interview residents about trip hazards and flooding risks

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge Broadly
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints exploded to 258 filings THIS WEEK versus 37.4 weekly average (590% spike, z-score 5.44), while park noise jumped 967% to 4 complaints this week versus 0.4 baseline (z-score 5.21), suggesting possible event, construction, or behavioral shift.
evidence: 258 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 37.4 weekly average (590% increase, z-score 5.44)
4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% increase, z-score 5.21)
Noise complaints are already endemic (1,423 residential, 794 street/sidewalk over 90 days), suggesting concentrated new source or event
reporting_angles: Identify major events, construction projects, or venue openings in Flushing's downtown core this week that could drive noise spike
Interview residents in high-complaint zones (likely around Flushing Commons development and Flushing Park); assess quality-of-life impact

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes and Micro-Mobility Clutter
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints surged to 3 filings THIS WEEK from a 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69), while bike/roller/skate obstruction spiked 1100% two weeks ago (z-score 6.35), indicating potential dockless bike system collapse or enforcement gap.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% increase, z-score 8.69)
3 bike/roller/skate complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 baseline (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Flushing's densely populated commercial corridors create visibility for micro-mobility clutter; suggests either vendor neglect or inadequate city enforcement
reporting_angles: Contact bike-share operators (Citibike, etc.) about service levels and abandoned unit collection in Flushing; verify if system is experiencing operational issues
Document sidewalk obstruction with photos; assess impact on ADA accessibility and pedestrian flow on Main Street/Northern Boulevard

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster (Earlier Signal)
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints peaked 3 WEEKS AGO at 9 filings versus a 1.2 weekly baseline (620% spike, z-score 9.35), representing a moderate-aged but high-severity signal now subsiding; warrants retrospective investigation of food vendor practices.
evidence: 9 food poisoning complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (620% increase, z-score 9.35)
Signal is now aging (occurred 3 weeks prior); current week levels not provided but spike appears to have subsided
Flushing's dense restaurant and street food vendor ecosystem creates high exposure; cluster could indicate food handling lapses or contamination event
reporting_angles: FOIL DOHMH inspection records for the 3-week window; identify which vendors received violations for improper food handling in that period
Interview affected residents about symptoms and venues; cross-reference with health department outbreak investigation records
